title: Commit Window Protocol and Hot-Path Capacity Allocation
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Mid-cycle staffing shifts and unplanned spikes frequently cause scope churn and missed SLAs. We need a lightweight, repeatable protocol that lets PMs, Eng leads and EMs commit small capacity changes ("commit windows") while preserving predictability for cross-team launches and Dedicated capacity planning.

Goal: Define a Commit Window Protocol (CWP) and a Hot-Path Capacity Allocation matrix that: 1) standardizes when and how teams can request temporary capacity; 2) defines quantized scope buckets and rollback conditions; 3) provides an automated signal-to-decision flow that minimizes manual review for low-risk requests and routes higher-risk requests to the Capacity Board.

Scope: Protocol definition, decision matrix, monitoring signals, playbook for approvals and rollbacks, dashboard template for near-real-time capacity consumption, and a short pilot with 3 teams (Console, Serving Runtime, and Optimize). Not covering long-term financial re-commitments for Dedicated contracts (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: A documented CWP with step-by-step flow, approval tiers, and timing windows (doc in Confluence)
Decision matrix that maps request size, customer impact and latency risk to auto-approve / board-review / deny
Dashboard widget in Console that shows current committed vs available surge lanes and predicted runway for 72h
Pilot executed with 3 teams, at least 2 successful temporary allocations and one rollback exercise
Post-pilot retro with clear recommendations and a proposal for policy adoption for the next cycle
decisions: Adopt a rolling weekly commit window: requests submitted by EOD Monday are eligible for approval by Thursday EOD
Quantize requests into 3 buckets: small (<=10% team capacity), medium (10-30%), large (>30%)
Small requests auto-approve if no model change and estimated cost delta < $2000/month; medium require Engineering Lead + PM signoff; large go to Capacity Board
Hot-Path lanes will be tracked separately from Reserved/Dedicated capacity and have a defined rollback TTL (default 72 hours)
Integrate the CWP into the Console as a lightweight form and telemetry feed (showing predicted latencies and token throughput impact)
tradeoffs: Speed vs predictability: auto-approve for small requests speeds teams but risks unseen contention; mitigated by short TTLs and automated circuit-breakers
Simplicity vs coverage: Quantized buckets simplify decision-making but may misclassify complex workloads; pilot will surface adjustment needs
Operational overhead: Adding a Capacity Board increases governance but reduces cross-team conflicts for large commits
Cost transparency: setting dollar thresholds simplifies approvals but requires better cost estimation tooling (separate follow-up)
